items.title: Heart
items.summary: The heart is a hard-working, fist-sized muscle found in people and animals. It pumps out blood through tube-like structures called blood vessels.

items.title: Brain
items.summary: The brain is the part of the body which lets living beings think. It does some bodily functions, such as telling the rest of the body what to do.

items.title: Lung
items.summary: The lung is an organ in many vertebrates (animals having a spine, or backbone). It takes blood oxygen from the air, and expels carbon dioxide.

items.title: Human skeleton
items.summary: human skeleton is the internal framework of the body. It is made up of about 300 bones at birth.

items.title: Muscle
items.summary: Muscle is a tissue in animal bodies. Muscles are basically tissue which may contract (shorten).

items.title: Skin
items.summary: The skin is the outer covering of mammals and some other animals. It has many important jobs.

items.title: Eye
items.summary: The eye is a round organ for sensing light so organisms can see. It is the first part of the visual system.

items.title: Ear
items.summary: The ear is the part of the body which allows animals (including people) to hear. People and most mammals have ears.

items.title: Nose
items.summary: A nose is a body part which allows animals to smell things. The nose also helps animals breathe.

items.title: Stomach
items.summary: The stomach is part of the digestive system. It is an internal organ between the esophagus and the small intestines.

items.title: Liver
items.summary: The liver is an organ in the abdomen. It is part of the digestive system.

items.title: Blood
items.summary: Blood is a liquid in humans and many animals. There are about 5 litres of blood in the human body.

items.title: Bone
items.summary: Bones are parts of the skeleton of vertebrates. They also protect organs inside our body.

items.title: Tooth
items.summary: A tooth is one of the hard, white things in the mouth. Teeth (plural) are used to help the mastication process by chewing food.

items.title: Digestion
items.summary: Digestion is the process of breaking down food to absorb it. Food is broken down into smaller pieces, which are soluble in water.

items.title: Immune system
items.summary: The immune system is the set of tissues which work together to resist infections. The immune mechanisms help an organism identify a pathogen, and neutralize its threat.

items.title: Cell
items.summary: In biology, the cell is the basic structure of organisms. All living things are made up of cells, from the organs in the human body to the parts of plants.

items.title: DNA
items.summary: DNA, short for deoxyribonucleic acid, is the molecule that contains the genetic code of living organisms. This includes animals, plants, protists, archaea and bacteria.

items.title: Sleep
items.summary: Sleep (also called napping) is a state of resting. It happens in most animals, including humans.

items.title: Hair
items.summary: Hair is something that grows from the skin of mammals. Hair is made of keratins, which are proteins.

items.title: Vaccine
items.summary: A vaccine is a biological preparation. It is given to prevent a specific infectious or malignant disease.

items.title: Pancreas
items.summary: The pancreas is an organ that makes hormones and enzymes to help digestion. The pancreas helps break down carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.

items.title: Blood vessel
items.summary: A blood vessel is a tube that carries blood around the circulatory system. Blood vessels that take blood away from the heart are arteries.

items.title: Hormone
items.summary: Hormones are the chemical messengers of the endocrine system. Hormones are the signals which adjust the body's internal working, together with the nervous system.

items.title: Breathing
items.summary: Breathing is moving air in and out of the lungs. The air going in and out is called breath.

items.title: Taste
items.summary: Taste is one of the five main senses that helps people and animals enjoy and understand the food they eat. It allows us to notice different flavors, such as sweet, salty, sour, bitter, and umami (a savory taste).

items.title: Human body
items.summary: The human body is the body of a person. It is the physical structure of a person.

items.title: Artery
items.summary: An artery is a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart to other parts of the body. Almost all arteries carry blood with a lot of oxygen in it.

items.title: Thumb
items.summary: In human anatomy, the thumb is the first digit on a hand.

items.title: Leg
items.summary: A leg is a weight-bearing and locomotion device. Birds and humans have two legs, but many animals have four or six or even more.
